purpose: dataretrieval.waterdata: the USGS-maintained Python client for the Water Data OGC API. For code the agent writes itself; the aihydro tools use the aihydro-data adapter instead (usgs_waterdata card).

waterdata.get_daily.note: daily values; discharge is parameter_code '00060', mean statistic_id '00003'
waterdata.get_daily.returns: (DataFrame, metadata) tuple, like the other dataretrieval getters

waterdata.get_continuous.statistic: statistic_id '00011' (instantaneous); the daily mean '00003' applies to the daily collection only
waterdata.get_continuous.note: at most 3 years per query; timestamps are UTC

gotchas: Set API_USGS_PAT (an api.data.gov key) in the environment before heavy use: the service applies an hourly rate limit per key and answers HTTP 429 beyond it (see the dataretrieval README for the current limit).

Each getter returns a (DataFrame, metadata) tuple. With convert_type=True (the default) dataretrieval converts values to numbers and timestamps; only the raw API body carries values as strings and missing values as null, which is what the aihydro-data adapter parses and checks explicitly.
The legacy dataretrieval.nwis functions call waterservices.usgs.gov, decommissioned on 2027-02-22. Do not use them in new code.
approval_status (Approved / Provisional) and qualifier are separate fields; keep both with the values.
Discharge is in ft^3/s; convert with 0.028316846592 m^3 per ft^3.
